summary:
The model's sp and trends categories are the clear signal across every rating slice right now — all four ratings (R1-R4) are sitting at 7-1 (88%) on trends and sp over the last 14 days, with sp riding a 3-game win streak on every rating. That's not noise from one book; it's uniform across R1 through R4, and it pairs with the best combo in the data set: trends+sp hits 58% (370-268, n=638) over the full season. Compare that to bullpen_fatigue, which is ice cold everywhere — 3-5 (38%) over 14 days with a 5-game losing streak on all four ratings. Any pick today where bullpen_fatigue is the only category in favor should be faded hard; if trends and sp both back it, lean in with confidence.

For today's slate, that means scanning for games where R2 or R3 strong plays line up with trends+sp agreement — R2 is the hottest rating on recent strong-play units (14d 4-1, 80%, +3.0u; 30d 11-4, 73%, +9.0u), and R3 isn't far behind on season efficiency (+92.0u, 58% hit rate, best in the group). If either rating flags a strong play today, that's the one to size up. Watch the team context too: if MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD show up as the liked side, history is loud — LAD strong plays are 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) and BOS strong plays sit at 76% (+19.0u), both well clear of the field. NYY remains the one team to treat skeptically even when picked — 49% overall and a losing record on strong plays (9-14, -4.0u), so if NYY is today's "value" side, let the category agreement (or lack of it) break the tie rather than the team name. Bottom line: today's best spots are where sp/trends agreement meets a R2 or R3 strong play, ideally with BOS, LAD, TBR, or MIL on the right side of the number.
